title: Response-latency splitter: per-route/model p50/p95/p99 with IO-mode trace tags
creator: Maya Patel
description: Add a latency-splitting pipeline and dashboard views that break down end-to-end response time by model variant and user-facing route, with explicit IO-mode (streaming vs non-streaming) attribution. This ticket covers runtime trace hooks + metric enrichment, storage-side label mapping, percentile panels (p50/p95/p99) and SLI wiring for alerting. Goal: enable engineers and SREs to quickly surface regressions that only affect either streaming or non-streaming paths or specific model variants, and to attribute latency to fallback/compatibility paths (e.g., quantized fallback).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits trace & metric tags: route=<route>, model_variant=<family@version>, io_mode=streaming|non_streaming, cache_hit=true|false
Metrics pipeline preserves tags end-to-end and supports cardinality-safe rollouts (tag sampling configuration documented)
New Grafana dashboard with panels: p50/p95/p99 split by model_variant and by route, and a toggle to show IO-mode breakdown; panels must allow filtering by time window and service region
SLI definitions added: route-level latency SLI (p95 < SLO threshold) computed separately for streaming and non-streaming; alerts firing/tested in staging
Trace links from dashboard panels to trace viewer with the same tags pre-applied
Performance/regression test demonstrating metric ingestion cost within 10% of baseline for 30d retention with tag sampling turned on
Documentation (Confluence) describing rollout, rollback, and cardinality mitigations
work_items: Add trace-enrichment hook in serving runtime to annotate spans with route/model/io_mode/cache_hit
Update metric exporter to convert high-cardinality values (model full hash) to model_family@version tag by mapping table
Implement tag sampling in metrics pipeline and expose sampling config via infra flags
Create Grafana dashboard with percentile panels and streaming/non-streaming stacked bars
Wire SLI computation job and create alerting rules in staging
End-to-end test: generate synthetic workloads (streaming and blocking) and validate panels and alerts
Schedule a canary rollout (10% of hostnames) followed by 50% and global after 72h stable
notes: 2026-03-02: Spike complete. Added prototype hooks to runtime; initial tags emitted for route and io_mode. Observed 2% overhead on p99 in local microbenchmarks (acceptable).
2026-03-04: Decision: convert model full-hash to model_family@version at exporter to avoid explosion in metric series. Mapping table stored in config service (see PR 198).

2026-03-06: Trade-off discussion with SRE: higher cardinality gives signal but increases ingestion cost. Agreed on tag sampling default 10% for unknown model families, 100% for top 10 families. Documented in telemetry spec.

2026-03-08: QA ran synthetic streaming workload. Dashboard panels reflect expected p95 split; small discrepancy in p99 due to KV cache warm-up. Added a panel to show cache_hit ratio alongside latency.
2026-03-09: Security review: no PII in tags. KMS review not required. security_review_required:false noted.
2026-03-10: Preparing canary. Rollout plan updated: 10% -> 25% -> 100% over 5 days if no regression. Notify SRE channel on each step.
